_note: Gift a visit: a caregiver or a sponsor names one visit, for one named person, and pays nothing towards anybody else's. Money's contract for it, beside packages/catalog/apis/money.json, which holds the route and its refusal, and packages/catalog/vouchers.json, whose expiry and redemption arithmetic this reuses by import rather than by a second copy. packages/engines/src/money/domain/gifts.ts reads this file. Nothing here is a real service: no gift exists, nobody is named and no visit is booked.
_whyNotAVoucher: A voucher is a bearer code: whoever holds it spends it, on a visit or a plan they choose. A gift is not a bearer instrument at all — it is made out to one person by her own subject reference from the moment it is given, for one named visit, and it is never a code anybody could read out at a till. So it is its own kind here rather than a voucher with a name taped to it, and it reuses only what genuinely carries over: the catalogue price a visit is issued at, and how many years an unused one lasts, both packages/catalog/vouchers.json's own numbers, read from there rather than restated.
_whyNoNativeEmitter: Neither native app gives or books a gift in this wave — a giver and a beneficiary both act from the web preview, the same as a voucher's checkout. A generated Swift and Kotlin copy of this file would be a copy nobody renders, and a copy nobody renders is the one that drifts. The day a phone gives or books a gift, scripts/emit-gifts.mjs is written with the screen that reads it.

beneficiary.statement: A gift is made out to one person, by the account she already holds. Nobody else may spend it, and she may not hand it to somebody else.
beneficiary.why: Paying is not deciding when somebody is visited, and it is not deciding who is. A gift that anybody holding it could spend is a voucher, and this is not one.

bookingFieldWordsWhy: A request that names an appointment, a booking, or an agreement made on the beneficiary's behalf is refused as gift-books-for-them before anything is keyed. The giver names who and what; only the person receiving it books it, in her own account, and nothing here can carry a booking or her agreement in the same breath as the gift.

expiry.why: A gift and a voucher are both a prepaid amount towards a visit, held for somebody rather than spent at once, so Consumer Protection Act section 63 reaches both the same way. There is no second setting: a gift issued today lasts as long as a voucher issued today, read from the one place that number is decided.

preview.why: A fictional gift the web preview's ledger issues on the giver's screen so the beneficiary's screen, in the same tab, shows what the ledger answered rather than a row somebody typed. Lerato is the preview's patient throughout the app; Uncle Sipho is a sponsor role who has never appeared before this screen, because a gift needs a giver who is not already the treasurer of the preview's stokvel.
